document.title: The Boeing Company Spirit AeroSystems Acquisition Closing Release (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

tables.title: Spirit AeroSystems Acquisition Closing Perimeter and Segment Integration

disclosure.value: Boeing completed its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: SPR) effective December 8, 2025.

All of Spirit's Boeing-related commercial operations integrate under Commercial Airplanes (BCA), including 737 fuselages, major structures for 767, 777, and 787 Dreamliner, and commercially procured fuselages for P-8 and KC-46.

Spirit's aftermarket businesses align under Boeing Global Services (BGS), bringing Boeing's largest spare parts supplier in-house, expanding global MRO footprint, and adding to BGS's rotable, lease, and exchange portfolio.

Spirit Defense established as a non-integrated subsidiary of Boeing Defense, Space & Security (BDS); aligns with BDS for financial reporting and select enterprise functional/site support while maintaining independent governance and operations as an independent supplier to U.S. defense and space programs.
Acquired portions of Spirit AeroSystems' operations in Belfast, Northern Ireland operate as an independent subsidiary branded as Short Brothers, a Boeing Company.

Commercial and aftermarket operations in Wichita (Kansas), Dallas (Texas), Tulsa (Oklahoma), and Spirit's Aerospace Innovation Center in Prestwick (Scotland) begin integrating into Boeing alongside Belfast; approximately 15,000 teammates across the five sites join Boeing.
